style: Cinematic 16:9 graphic-novel still, painterly and sharp, muted olive, cigarette-gold, cold fluorescent teal, film grain, dramatic lighting. Recurring stylized Russian president (graphic-novel Putin-like figure, NOT a photograph): short pale thinning hair, lined pale face, thin mouth, small cold unsmiling eyes, dark navy suit. Recurring fictional American man: late thirties, short brown hair, weary small eyes, slightly oversized round cartoon head, not a celebrity. No readable text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, or captions.

jobs.line: I do not hate you.
jobs.scene: Extreme close-up of the stylized Russian president's cold eyes looking straight into the camera, lamp catching an iris, rain on glass behind him.

jobs.line: Hate would mean you counted as a person.
jobs.scene: He sits alone at a steel desk; across from him an empty chair where a person should be. The chair is weather, not a guest.

jobs.line: You are weather. A climate that repeats.
jobs.scene: A rain-lashed window, looping weather-radar circles on a glowing map, the president watching the same storm repeat.

jobs.line: I have been waiting you out since you had a flip phone.
jobs.scene: Younger Americans with flip phones in a 2000s mall, tiny in the rain-window reflection of the president who has been waiting.

jobs.line: Weather is not an enemy. Weather is a calendar.
jobs.scene: A wall calendar instead of a war map; the president's finger on a date, not a target. Weather as time.

jobs.line: You know my name.
jobs.scene: Americans on a phone screen mouthing his name; he does not look at the camera, he already knows.

jobs.line: I have known your type longer than you have had a passport.
jobs.scene: A pile of expired passports on his desk; he has been cataloguing this type since before the ink faded.

jobs.line: The first American I ever met was not a person. It was a commercial.
jobs.scene: A CRT television blasting a toothpaste-and-soda commercial; the president watching it like a briefing, not like TV.

jobs.line: White teeth. A red cup the size of a head.
jobs.scene: Giant white teeth and a huge sweating red cup filling the TV frame, grotesque, American, too bright.

jobs.line: A family hugging in a kitchen so bright it has to be fake, because it is.
jobs.scene: A too-bright fake kitchen, family frozen mid-hug under studio lights, cables on the linoleum, the president's silhouette in the doorway.

jobs.line: That is not entertainment to me.
jobs.scene: He turns away from the TV, unimpressed; the commercial is a document, not a joke.

jobs.line: That is your self-portrait, sold back to you at scale.
jobs.scene: Billboard of the American man's face sold back as a product, endless copies receding down a highway at night.

jobs.line: You talk in restaurants like the room is empty.
jobs.scene: Crowded diner, the American man shouting with both hands, other diners recoiling, the president observing from a dark booth.

jobs.line: You ask a stranger their job before their name.
jobs.scene: The American pumps a stranger's hand over a buffet, asking a job before a name, name-tag still face-down.

jobs.line: You wear the logo on purpose.
jobs.scene: Close on a hoodie chest with a huge unreadable brand mark worn like a uniform, on purpose.

jobs.line: In the classroom they still draw you with a flag on the sleeve and no idea where Kaliningrad is.
jobs.scene: A drab classroom chalkboard: stick-figure American with a sleeve flag, a world map with a blank hole where Kaliningrad should be.

jobs.line: That drawing is not an insult. It is an operating assumption.
jobs.scene: The president underlines the chalkboard drawing in a dossier. Not insult. Operating assumption. Red pencil.

jobs.line: I log the smile.
jobs.scene: His hand stamps a photocopied American smile onto an index card. Logging it.

jobs.line: You smile at cameras, at cashiers, at people who have not earned it.
jobs.scene: The American grinning at a cashier who does not smile back; cameras; unearned warmth. The president takes notes in shadow.

jobs.line: In my notes a smile is a tell:
jobs.scene: Dossier page: a smile circled, labelled in the president's mind as a tell. Close on the circle, not on letters.

jobs.line: you want to be liked more than you want to win.
jobs.scene: The American nodding too fast in a meeting, palms open, needing to be liked, losing.

jobs.line: I watch your movies the way a surgeon watches an X-ray.
jobs.scene: The president as a surgeon at an X-ray lightbox, but the film is a Hollywood still. Clinical. Cold.

jobs.line: The hero who breaks the rules and is rewarded. The president who is secretly good.
jobs.scene: Cinema screen: a rule-breaking hero rewarded under fireworks; a secretly-good president at a podium. Empty theatre, one watcher.

jobs.line: The war that ends in a speech.
jobs.scene: A wooden podium, a war ending in a speech, ticker-tape, no soldiers left on the stage. Hollow victory lighting.

jobs.line: I do not believe the movies. I believe that you do.
jobs.scene: Split: the president unmoved in the dark; the American in the front row, mouth open, believing every frame.

jobs.line: By the time you walk into a real room,
jobs.scene: The American in a rumpled jacket waiting in a panelled anteroom, about to enter, clock with no numbers.

jobs.line: the cartoon is already sitting in the other chair.
jobs.scene: He sits down. The other chair already holds a cardboard tourist in shorts. The cartoon arrived first.

jobs.line: You will spend the first twenty minutes fighting a drawing of yourself.
jobs.scene: The American jabbing a finger at the cardboard cutout, arguing with a drawing of himself, twenty minutes on the clock.

jobs.line: Most of you never notice.
jobs.scene: His shoe tapping under the table, unaware. The president watches through a barely open door.

jobs.line: The second folder is thinner, and it cost more to build.
jobs.scene: A thinner, more expensive folder placed on the desk beside the fat one. Gold clip. Cost.

jobs.line: It is not about what you say. It is about what you buy.
jobs.scene: Not a speech: a pile of receipts and a credit-card slip. What you buy. The president's hand on the receipts.

jobs.line: You will sell a principle for a cheaper flight.
jobs.scene: Airport kiosk, the American choosing the cheapest flight, a crumpled principle in the bin.

jobs.line: You will sell a friendship for a better rate.
jobs.scene: Cafe handshake, a better rate on a napkin, friendship cooling in two cups. The American taking it.

jobs.line: You will sell a secret, I am certain, for a feeling:
jobs.scene: A small card that only feels like a feeling, held over a closed wallet. The secret is not money yet.

jobs.line: being the smartest man at a table of people who already know.
jobs.scene: The American leaning in at a dinner table of men who already exchanged a look. He needs to be the cleverest.

jobs.line: Money is the lazy tool. I do not lead with money.
jobs.scene: A dusty closed cash box ignored; a velvet rope labelled access in the president's gesture, no letters.

jobs.line: I lead with access.
jobs.scene: The president opening a door marked only by light: access. The American stepping toward it, hungry.

jobs.line: A conference in Vienna. A think-tank panel.
jobs.scene: Vienna conference foyer, marble, think-tank banner with no readable words, the American clutching a programme.

jobs.line: A private dinner where someone important remembered your paper.
jobs.scene: Candlelit dinner, the American lighting up as an older host mentions his paper. Ego, wine, heavy drapes.

jobs.line: Ego is cheaper than cash, and it does not show up on a bank statement.
jobs.scene: Bank statement with nothing unusual; a dinner invite beside it. Ego cheaper than a wire. The president almost smiles.

jobs.line: You think of yourself as a citizen. I think of you as a market.
jobs.scene: Split street: voting booth vs market stall. The American as citizen on the left, as product on the right.

jobs.line: Markets have seasons. Markets punish hesitation.
jobs.scene: Market chalkboard of seasons, a gavel of hesitation. Prices changing. The president as the stall's shadow.

jobs.line: Markets, above all,
jobs.scene: Wide market, rain, the stall waiting. 'Above all' hanging in the air as weather.

jobs.line: come back after they crash and ask for the same product with a new slogan.
jobs.scene: A crashed toy cart glued back with a new slogan sticker. Same dented wheel. The American returning with a bag.

jobs.line: That is the most useful sentence I have on you.
jobs.scene: The president's finger on one underlined sentence in the folder. The useful sentence. Close.

jobs.line: You come back.
jobs.scene: The American walking back into the same shop, same product, new bag. The clerk unsurprised. The president already knew.

jobs.line: I respect the hardware.
jobs.scene: The president nodding once at scale models of carriers on a planning table. Respect, private, no smile.

jobs.line: I will tell you that in private, and I am not lying.
jobs.scene: Two men at a night window, one is the president, thermos, city grid, telling the truth about hardware.

jobs.line: Carriers. Satellites. A budget that looks like a hallucination when you write it in rubles.
jobs.scene: Carrier models, satellite dishes, a budget spilling off the page next to ruble notes. Hallucination of money.

jobs.line: I do not respect the will.
jobs.scene: A steel I-beam standing; a slack frayed rope beside it. Hardware vs will. The president looking at the rope.

jobs.line: That is the split. Everything after it hangs on that split.
jobs.scene: A dossier split down the middle, a crack in the table. Everything hanging on that crack.

jobs.line: I counted the years in Afghanistan. I counted the years in Iraq.
jobs.scene: Wall calendar with years X'd out, two country names as shapes not letters. Afghanistan, Iraq, counted.

jobs.line: I counted how long a democracy argues with itself before the arguing becomes the mission.
jobs.scene: A brightly lit parliament arguing while a mission clock runs. The arguing IS the mission. The president checking a stopwatch.

jobs.line: I have a number for that. I have tested it.
jobs.scene: Chalkboard with a single number underlined, then TESTED. Chalk dust on the president's sleeve.

jobs.line: You will bomb a mountain. You will not occupy a winter.
jobs.scene: Snow mountain, one smoke puff, no boots on the slope. Bomb yes, occupy winter no.

jobs.line: You will announce a red line, and then hold a hearing about the announcement.
jobs.scene: A red line drawn on a speech, then a hearing gavel in the next room through an open door. Announcement about the announcement.

jobs.line: I do not need you weak. I need you busy.
jobs.scene: The president at a window: he does not need the American weak. He needs him busy. Three TVs of crises behind him.

jobs.line: A superpower with three crises and a midterm is, to me,
jobs.scene: Situation room, three crisis screens plus a campaign poster on a fourth. Midterm. Planners sipping tea, unhurried.

jobs.line: a superpower with no crises at all.
jobs.scene: The same room emptied of urgency. A superpower with no crises at all, because it is busy. Tea steam.

jobs.line: The soldier in my folder is not a coward.
jobs.scene: A soldier in a file photo, standing still in kit, tired, not afraid, not a coward. The president holding the photo.

jobs.line: He is a man whose country will bring him home the moment the pictures get bad.
jobs.scene: Transport plane ramp, duffel already on, news photos of a bad street on a table. Home the moment pictures get bad.

jobs.line: I plan around the pictures. I plan around the fact that you have evening news.
jobs.scene: The president's finger on a TV bezel showing evening news. Plan around the pictures. Plan around the fact you have one.

jobs.line: This is the page I underline.
jobs.scene: A dossier page so underlined the paper fibres are fuzzy. This page. Red pencil broken.

jobs.line: You replace the entire foreign policy of a nuclear state the way other countries replace a cabinet minister.
jobs.scene: Movers swapping an entire wall of maps in a nuclear briefing room in one morning. Foreign policy as furniture.

jobs.line: On a Tuesday. With a parade.
jobs.scene: Tuesday parade, confetti, a treaty binder riding a float. Cabinet-minister replacement energy.

jobs.line: A treaty is not a treaty. It is a mood.
jobs.scene: Treaty binder with a sticky January expiry, gold seal loose. A mood, not a treaty.

jobs.line: A mood that expires in January.
jobs.scene: Wall calendar, JANUARY circled until the paper tears. The mood expires. The president already flipped the page.

jobs.line: I do not take your word. I take your calendar.
jobs.scene: Not a handshake: a calendar. The president taking the calendar, leaving the word on the table.

jobs.line: How many months until your election. How many months until the other party's primary.
jobs.scene: Three columns of months-until: election, primary, committee. The shortest starred. His pencil.

jobs.line: How many months until the man who shook my hand is explaining himself to a committee.
jobs.scene: Chandelier handshake, then the same man under fluorescent committee lights explaining. The president in the gallery shadow.

jobs.line: You think consistency is a virtue.
jobs.scene: A marble bust labelled consistency in the American's mind, a crack already down the cheek. He thinks it is a virtue.

jobs.line: I think consistency is a problem I do not have to have with you.
jobs.scene: The president shrugging at a chart of broken timelines, coffee, snow window. Consistency is not his problem with you.

jobs.line: The useful move is not to convince you.
jobs.scene: He waits. Clock. Empty chairs. Not convincing you — waiting. A spider patience.

jobs.line: It is to wait until you convince yourselves of the opposite of whatever you said last year.
jobs.scene: The American on TV arguing the opposite of last year's speech, old clip paused on a second screen. He convinces himself.

jobs.line: You are very good at that. You call it a mandate.
jobs.scene: Campaign button, wet glue, recycled slogan. Mandate. The American proud. The president unimpressed.

jobs.line: Somewhere in a room with bad heating, a date gets written next to a name.
jobs.scene: Shabby office, steam pipes, visible breath, bad heating. A date written next to a name. Gloved hand.

jobs.line: The date is Inauguration Day. The name is whoever you just elected.
jobs.scene: Inauguration bunting through a small window; on the desk the new name, same folder. Whoever you just elected.

jobs.line: The folder does not change. Only the heading does.
jobs.scene: Same fat folder, new paper title strip, old strip in the trash. Contents unchanged. Only the heading.

jobs.line: I do not need to invent your arguments. You publish them. You fund them.
jobs.scene: Op-eds and a donate-button laptop clipped into his folder. Your arguments, published, funded, his.

jobs.line: You put them on the internet with a donate button.
jobs.scene: A glowing donate button, the American clicking it, funding his own opposition research for free.

jobs.line: A university panel about your own decline.
jobs.scene: University panel, decline banner blank, nearly empty chairs, the American at the mic nodding along.

jobs.line: A journalist who hates the Pentagon more than he hates the tanks.
jobs.scene: Journalist at a messy desk, Pentagon badge in a drawer, tank photo face-down, cursor blinking with more hate for home.

jobs.line: A celebrity reading a statement about a war they could not find on a map an hour ago.
jobs.scene: Celebrity at a podium reading a statement, folded war map still in the assistant's bag. Cameras firing.

jobs.line: The choir is not secret. The choir has a mailing list.
jobs.scene: Mailing-list printout, rubber stamp SECRET crossed out. The choir is not secret. Names as grey bars.

jobs.line: In the old building we used to plant stories. Now we retweet.
jobs.scene: Old telegram spike next to a glowing phone with a retweet arrow. Same dusty office. Then and now.

jobs.line: The skill is the same: find the American already angry at America,
jobs.scene: An already-angry American; the president's unseen hand pushing a larger microphone toward him.

jobs.line: and give him a bigger room.
jobs.scene: The angry American in a huge hall, spotlight, bigger room, taking it. The president in the back row, small.

jobs.line: You call this a marketplace of ideas. I call it a buffet.
jobs.scene: Marketplace stall of idea-posters vs a buffet of the same posters with spoons. The American filling a plate.

jobs.line: I do not have to be the chef.
jobs.scene: Chef's hat on a hook, buffet lid open, no cook. The president is not the chef. He is a guest at the right hour.

jobs.line: I only have to be hungry at the right hour.
jobs.scene: Wall clock at a hungry hour, fork on a manifesto, crumbs. The president sitting down to eat.

jobs.line: The most valuable American in the folder is not a spy.
jobs.scene: Spy coat on a hanger, empty. A name tag that is not the valuable American. Not a spy.

jobs.line: It is a sincere person.
jobs.scene: Sincere American at a kitchen table, webcam light, no handler, believing every word. The most valuable.

jobs.line: Sincere people do not need to be recruited. They need to be amplified.
jobs.scene: The same sincere man amplified onto a huge public screen, still in kitchen clothes, night. Amplified, not recruited.

jobs.line: They will do the rest on their own time, in their own voice,
jobs.scene: He keeps talking in his own voice at his own table. The president's budget: zero. Timesheet empty.

jobs.line: at no cost to my budget.
jobs.scene: A cost of zero stamped on a closed folder. No envelope yet. The work is already free.

jobs.line: If you are waiting for a villain in a dark coat to hand someone an envelope,
jobs.scene: Park bench, frost, dark coat, sealed envelope unused. The villain you were waiting for. Empty.

jobs.line: you have misunderstood the century.
jobs.scene: A century misunderstood: the bench in daylight, the coat gone, only a quote left behind.

jobs.line: The envelope is a quote. The quote is yours.
jobs.scene: Envelope opened: a printed quote in the American's own type. The quote is yours. The president does not need to write it.

jobs.line: The Americans I actually drink with are not the cartoon.
jobs.scene: Mayfair hotel bar, quiet Americans in dark coats, no logos. The president drinking with them, not with the cartoon.

jobs.line: They are the ones in Mayfair. In Geneva.
jobs.scene: Geneva lakeside dusk, brass plaque, black car. Then the same coats. Quiet money.

jobs.line: On a yacht registered nowhere and docked everywhere.
jobs.scene: White yacht, blank stern, no flag, champagne, grey harbour. Registered nowhere, docked everywhere.

jobs.line: They speak quietly. They know where the money sits when it is tired of flags.
jobs.scene: Two men speaking softly over untouched whiskey; tired little paper flags in an ashtray. Money sitting still.

jobs.line: They will lecture a camera about democracy at lunch.
jobs.scene: The quiet American lecturing a camera about democracy at lunch, boom mic, perfect daylight, the president off-camera.

jobs.line: And ask at dinner whether the sanction list has a loophole with a name on it.
jobs.scene: Same man at dinner, candlelight, asking about a sanction loophole, a name inside a matchbook. The president listening.

jobs.line: This is the most dangerous page, because it is the most intimate.
jobs.scene: The folder's most dangerous page, dog-eared, a fingerprint, intimate. The president's hand flat on it.

jobs.line: It says you are not a people. You are two countries sharing a language.
jobs.scene: A torn page split down the middle, two columns, one language. Not a people. Two countries.

jobs.line: One of them votes. One of them invoices.
jobs.scene: Voting queue on one pavement, invoicing office on the other, same street, rain. Votes vs invoices.

jobs.line: I have watched a senator's son sit at a table his father could not be seen at.
jobs.scene: Young man at a private table his father could not be seen at, waiter blocking the view, heavy curtains. The president in the corner.

jobs.line: I do not moralize about it. Moralizing is your hobby.
jobs.scene: He does not lecture. Moralizing is a hobbyhorse in a playroom while the work happens through an office door.

jobs.line: This American is not a hypocrite. Hypocrisy would require a standard.
jobs.scene: Dictionary with hypocrite crossed out, professional written in, a standard missing from the page.

jobs.line: This American is a professional. Professionals can be scheduled.
jobs.scene: Diary, professionals in ink, fifteen-minute slots. Schedulable. The president's finger on a time.

jobs.line: The cartoon is for television. This one is for the work.
jobs.scene: TV studio still using the cartoon tourist; cut to the quiet suit at a real desk in rain. Television vs work.

jobs.line: I have a cleaner word for your politics than you do.
jobs.scene: The president at the window, finding a cleaner word. Not politics. Something mechanical. His breath on glass.

jobs.line: I call it a machine.
jobs.scene: A huge voting machine, jam lights, oil on the floor. He names it: machine.

jobs.line: Machines have tolerances. Machines jam.
jobs.scene: Tolerance marks scratched on the housing. Then a jam. Gears seizing. Same machine.

jobs.line: Machines, if you study them long enough, make the same noise before they fail.
jobs.scene: A needle gauge in the red, the same noise every time before failure. The president's ear close, eyes closed, studying.

jobs.line: Fifty percent plus one. That is the whole religion.
jobs.scene: Ballot boxed as religion: fifty percent plus one. Truth and competence crossed out as grey bars.

jobs.line: Not truth. Not competence.
jobs.scene: Two discarded idols: a small statue of truth, a small statue of competence, in the skip. Not the religion.

jobs.line: Fifty percent plus one,
jobs.scene: The stamp slamming: fifty percent plus one.

jobs.line: and then four years of the winner pretending the loser was never real.
jobs.scene: Winner at a podium pretending the loser never existed; loser's portrait already in a skip. Four-year banner. The president watching.

jobs.line: I do not need to pick your president. I need to pick your argument.
jobs.scene: Not a president's face on the board: an ARGUMENT circled. He does not pick your president. He picks the fight.

jobs.line: An argument that lasts from August to November is a strategic pause I did not have to pay for.
jobs.scene: Street of yard signs August to November, a parked van, unpaid pause. Strategic, free. The president in the van.

jobs.line: You think I want you divided. That is too flattering.
jobs.scene: The American accusing him of wanting division, flattered, finger out. The president almost amused.

jobs.line: Division is a side effect.
jobs.scene: A tiny side-effect label on a bottle, while the real drug is attention. Division in small type.

jobs.line: What I want is your attention spent inward. On each other. On a clip.
jobs.scene: Phone clip on loop, two faces arguing in the reflection, inward. The president wants that glow, not the border.

jobs.line: On a man in a supermarket who said the wrong thing into a phone.
jobs.scene: Supermarket aisle, ordinary man saying the wrong thing into a phone, camera already there, cereal. Hearing-room energy in grocery light.

jobs.line: A country staring at itself cannot stare at a border.
jobs.scene: A country as an eye staring into a bathroom mirror; a border fence out of focus behind the glass. Cannot stare at both.

jobs.line: I have measured this. I will keep measuring it.
jobs.scene: Ruler and notebook, tally marks, MEASURED, then again. The president's hand making another mark.

jobs.line: Every time your news cycle eats a week, someone else's map gets a new road.
jobs.scene: News-cycle week eating a wall calendar; another country's map gaining a new red road. Trade.

jobs.line: The machine is not evil in the folder. Evil is a movie word.
jobs.scene: Movie-marquee EVIL unplugged; a plainer lamp on the folder. Not evil. A movie word. The president prefers the lamp.

jobs.line: The machine is predictable.
jobs.scene: The machine, still, humming, predictable. Close on gears that always do this.

jobs.line: Predictable is the highest compliment I give an enemy.
jobs.scene: He stamps the enemy file with the highest compliment: predictable. No smile. Highest compliment.

jobs.line: A new American walks onto a stage and talks about reset. About strength.
jobs.scene: New American on a stage, reset, strength, teleprompter, fresh paint over old slogans. The president in the wings, unmoved.

jobs.line: About a line that will not be crossed this time.
jobs.scene: A red line on a speech page, THIS TIME, ink wet. The new man believes it. The president does not.

jobs.line: I do not cheer. I do not panic. I open the same folder.
jobs.scene: Bad-heating room, steam, sweaters, kettle. He does not cheer. He does not panic. He opens the same folder.

jobs.line: The cartoon is still in it. The price tag. The soldier who goes home.
jobs.scene: Tabs still there: cartoon, price, soldier. Photographs swapped. His hands. Same tabs.

jobs.line: The headings have not moved in thirty years. Only the photographs have.
jobs.scene: Wall of headings unmoved thirty years, only photos changed, dust on the rails. He walks the rail.

jobs.line: I do not need you to be worse. I need you to be you.
jobs.scene: He looks at the American as he is, not worse: loud coat, watch-check. I need you to be you.

jobs.line: Loud. Rich. Impatient.
jobs.scene: Luxury watch, loud zipper, tapping impatient finger. Loud. Rich. Impatient. Three close-ups, one man.

jobs.line: Convinced that history is a sequel in which you still have the best effects budget.
jobs.scene: History as a sequel poster, best effects budget, the American first in line, popcorn, believing the trailer.

jobs.line: You will ask, at the end of a video like this, whether I am right.
jobs.scene: The American at the end of a video, facing a dark screen, asking if the man in the folder is right. His own reflection.

jobs.line: That question is also in the folder. Americans love a verdict.
jobs.scene: That question already ticked in the folder. Americans love a verdict. Checkbox. The president does not look up.

jobs.line: You love to put yourselves on the scale and argue with the reading.
jobs.scene: Bathroom scale, the American arguing with the number. The folder uninterested in the reading.

jobs.line: The folder does not care about the verdict.
jobs.scene: The folder does not care about the verdict. Close on the closed cover, indifferent.

jobs.line: It cares that you watched. That you felt seen, or insulted.
jobs.scene: A tiny tick: you watched. Seen or insulted, both possible. A pencil hovering. Cooling mug.

jobs.line: And that tomorrow you will argue about it with each other instead of looking up.
jobs.scene: Tomorrow: comment-bright room, Americans arguing with each other, nobody looking up at the dark window. The president at the window.

jobs.line: Someone new is already writing a speech about how this time will be different.
jobs.scene: Someone new writing a speech, coffee, blank page already lying. This time will be different. The president does not need to watch.

jobs.line: In the room with the bad heating, I sharpen a pencil.
jobs.scene: Bad-heating room, he sharpens a pencil over a bin of shavings, same length as last time. His hands. His ritual.

jobs.line: The cycle does not continue because I am brilliant.
jobs.scene: Not brilliance: a well-worn shoe print in the same puddle. The cycle. He is not performing genius.

jobs.line: It continues because you are familiar.
jobs.scene: The familiar American walking the same looping street again. That is why it continues. The president already seated at the desk, waiting.
